questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds contain all the carbon atoms in the same hybridisation state
questions.solution:
Key idea $pi$-bond do not participate in hybridisation

In H−C≡C−C=−H all carbon atoms are in same hybridization state i.e., sp​ hybridized.

a. $H - \overset{sp}{C} ≡ \overset{sp}{C} - \overset{sp}{C} ≡ \overset{sp}{C} - H$

b. $\overset{{sp}^{3}}{{CH}_{3}} - \overset{sp}{C} ≡ \overset{sp}{C} - \overset{{sp}^{3}}{{CH}_{3}}$

c. $\mathop{{CH}_{2}}_{{sp}^{2}} = \mathop{C}_{sp} = \overset{{sp}^{2}}{{CH}_{2}}$

d. $\mathop{{CH}_{2}}_{{sp}^{2}} = \mathop{CH -}_{{sp}^{2}}\mathop{C}_{sp} ≡ \mathop{CH}_{sp}$

questions.q:
Consider the following sequence of reactions.

$Z\overset{PCl5}{→}X\overset{Alc. KOH}{→}Y\mathop{→}_{2{H}_{2}O / \Delta}^{Conc. {H}_{2}{SO}_{4}}Z$

$' Z '$& is
questions.solution:
When ${CH}_{3}{CHOHCH}_{3}$ is reacted with ${PCl}_{5}$, 2-Chloropropane is formed. Thus, X is 2-Chloropropane ${CH}_{3}{CHClCH}_{3}$.

When ${CH}_{3}{CHOHCH}_{3}$ is reacted with alc. KOH , Propene& is formed. Thus, Y is ${CH}_{3} - CH = {CH}_{2}$.

When ${CH}_{3} - CH = {CH}_{2}$ is treated with conc. ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ and ${H}_{2}O$, 2-Propanol ${CH}_{3}{CHOHCH}_{3}$ is formed. Thus Z is ${CH}_{3}{CHOHCH}_{3}$.

questions.q: Which one of the following reactions is expected to readily give a hydrocarbon product in good yields?
questions.solution:
Electrolysis of a concentrated aqueous solution of either sodium or potassium salts of saturated carboxylic acids yields higher alkane at anode.



2 $\mathrm{RCOOK} \underset{\text{ Oxidation }}{\text{ Electrolytic }}{\longrightarrow} \underset{\text{ Anode }}{2 \mathrm{RCOO}^{-}}+\underset{\text{ Cathod }}{2 \mathrm{~K}^{+}}$At anode $2 \mathrm{RCOO}^{-} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{RCOO}+2 \mathrme^{-} \longrightarrow\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{R}+$2 $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$At Cathode $2 \mathrm{~K}^{+}+2 \mathrme^{-} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{~K}$

2 $\mathrm{~K}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} \rightarrow$2 $\mathrm{KOH}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \uparrow



($Kolbe's Method)
